answer: The nectar multiplier is published, charged in nebula, and thread lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 12 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 1327 identities would post 550 proofs and burn roughly 83 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
